title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: bullseye routing with user groups expands the eligible pool as wait time grows
notes: claim 64: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents Dataverse operations for user groups and playbook records, contrary to the briefing's automation gaps. The rollout checklist also misstates the wait-time rules, and the risk rationale asserts a data-access boundary the sources do not establish.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: API absence; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for creating conversation orchestration playbooks.
claims.quote: CC User Prompt (msdyn_ccuserprompt) ... Create ... POST /msdyn_ccuserprompts
claims.fix: Replace the blanket playbook API absence with 'Microsoft documents POST /msdyn_ccuserprompts to create CC User Prompt records; the conversation orchestration migration article identifies CC User Prompt as its playbook component. A publishing operation is not established by that table reference.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/developer/reference/entities/msdyn_ccuserprompt and the existing orchestration article. Keep controls[0].api null only for the combined create-and-publish operation, with a note narrowing the gap to publishing; remove the claim that playbooks are admin-centre-only.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: API absence; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for user groups.
claims.quote: Agent Group (msdyn_agentgroup) ... Create ... POST /msdyn_agentgroups
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api with kind 'rest', call 'POST /msdyn_agentgroups', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/developer/reference/entities/msdyn_agentgroup'. Narrow its note to say this creates the group record, with msdyn_name and msdyn_description; it is not the complete member-and-queue setup. The Queue User Group Membership reference explicitly identifies its msdyn_usergroup lookup as 'User Group (Agent Group)' targeting msdyn_agentgroup. Remove the blanket no-user-group-API assertion and narrow the open question to complete membership setup.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for editing or deleting playbooks.
claims.quote: Delete ... DELETE /msdyn_ccuserprompts(msdyn_ccuserpromptid) ... Update ... PATCH /msdyn_ccuserprompts(msdyn_ccuserpromptid)
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api to kind 'rest', call 'DELETE /msdyn_ccuserprompts(<msdyn_ccuserpromptid>)', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/developer/reference/entities/msdyn_ccuserprompt'. Note that this deletes the CC User Prompt record identified by the orchestration article as the playbook component; do not claim that generic record updates publish routing changes. Remove the broad no-playbook-API assertion.

claims.fix: Remove 'and reads no new organisational data' from the risk rationale. The narrower body statement that the template article describes no new data source can remain.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: The governance checklist names consumption-based billing and diagnostics checks without corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: Confirm the licensing and consumption-based billing prerequisites ... Review diagnostics with the custom query Learn references. ... Controls cover playbook creation, user groups, and playbook editing or deletion.
claims.fix: The Before rollout consumption-based billing check and After rollout diagnostics check have no corresponding controls-table rows. Do not invent paths or calls for them in this correction.

claims.claim: Administrators should apply a 30-second minimum and a 10-second increment between levels.
claims.quote: Sets the minimum wait time to at least 30 seconds. The next level wait time can be the same as the previous level or should increment by at least 10 seconds. Note that Level 1 also supports a 0 second wait time.
claims.fix: Replace 'remember the 30-second minimum and the 10-second increment between levels' with 'the minimum wait time is 30 seconds except that Level 1 also supports 0 seconds; a later level can use the same wait time as the preceding level or increase it by at least 10 seconds'.
